Thanks — I reviewed MedTech's RFI and sketched proposed contract language plus an acceptance checklist (attached). Key points below.

1) Evidence acceptance: minimal acceptable items (we should offer a tiered approach).
   - Tier A (preferred): Live witness session + sealed snapshot deposit. Deliverables: (a) sealed snapshot file deposit with SHA-256 checksum; (b) signed witness statement from Redwood Operator; (c) operations runbook excerpt covering deployment/rollback procedures.
   - Tier B (alternate): Remote demonstration + environment image hash + signed deployment log.
   - Acceptance criteria must include timestamped artifacts and an explicit chain-of-custody statement.

2) MSA / Order Form language (high level recommendation):
   - Add a new Exhibit G (Evidence & Operator Attestation) that defines delivery artifacts, timelines ("within 10 business days of Effective Date"), and acceptable substitutes.
   - License scope: clarify that the license grants runtime execution rights for the agreed environment only; prohibit model redistribution and separate developer access.
   - Indemnity carveouts: avoid broad language requiring Redwood to hold custody beyond a demonstrable deposit or signed attestation. Instead propose a limited witness-and-deposit model.

3) Redlines attached: MSA_Redline_v3.pdf highlights specific clauses; Evidence_Checklist_v2.xlsx is the checklist we can share with the customer.

Operational questions: David / Ben — please confirm whether a sealed snapshot + operator witness is operationally reasonable within 7 business days, and what the remote witness process would look like (video + recorded hash comparison, who signs). Also please note any security constraints (KMS/HSM key transfer limitations) that might affect wording.

If that all looks good, I suggest we: (a) share the Evidence_Checklist_v2.xlsx with MedTech, (b) propose Exhibit G text inline in the Order Form draft, and (c) offer a 30m call to finalize acceptance options.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
